subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single compact TypeScript module for a heavy 6-wheel armoured hauler—cab, sealed cargo pod with glowing seals and hazard decals, roof turret, side plating, neon accents, and a screen—aiming to keep the build around 300 lines using the designated SDK builder functions.

Working out exact dimensions and joint placement for chassis, wheels, cab, and cargo pod...

Checking vertex alignment between the cylinder and torus segments, I'll simplify by going with a 12-sided cylinder at radius 1.2 and a 12-segment torus at matching radius, rotated to align the facets.

Now I'm planning the pod's end caps using tapered cylinder geometry for the rear and front, mounted on saddle-shaped cradle boxes. For details, I'm adding a rear door with a biohazard/sealed emblem decal texture, plus flat decal panels on the cab sides since the round pod body isn't ideal for flat textures.

Working out the pod shape as an octagonal prism instead, computing the right radius and rotation so the flats face outward, then placing raised side-plate boxes that follow the curved surface offset.

For the guard theme, I'm settling on a roof turret with twin guns, side rocket pods, a spiked ram bumper, armor plates, roof light bar, and antenna — skipping the drone idea to keep things simpler. For body paint, I'm planning to write custom panel-line and worn-paint noise effects rather than importing a premade texture.

Color palette: dark steel-blue body, magenta and cyan accents, hazard yellow, and near-black trim. The front bumper gets hazard chevron stripes, flanks and underglow get neon rod lighting, and the windscreen uses dark cyan glass with a glowing visor strip. Now I'm writing helper functions for boxes and cylinders to construct the geometry.

Working out the six-wheel layout: front axle and rear tandem axle positions along z, wheel spacing along x so they sit just outside the narrower lower chassis but tucked under fenders attached to the wider cab deck, adjusting wheel center x to 1.35 so they clear the body without clipping.

Now I'm detailing each wheel assembly -- tyre cylinder, steel rim, a glowing cyan ring on the outer face, and small lug bolts, skipping tread detail for simplicity. I'm also setting up the joint hierarchy: hinge joints for each wheel parented to the chassis, a spine joint for the chassis root, and starting on the turret with yaw and pitch joints plus a gun barrel.

For the cab, I'm planning glowing grille slits, headlights, a roof lightbar, mirrors, and exhaust stacks mounted beside the pod, working out exact placement so they clear the cab roof and pod radius. I'm also sketching the nose as a tapered frustum shape extending forward from the cab.

Now I'm laying out the cab itself as a lower body box topped with an upper greenhouse box, positioning each with specific dimensions and offsets, plus a tilted glass windscreen at the front.

Still building the vehicle geometry...

Still working out cap rotations...

Now I'm adding glowing seal bands as toruses spaced along the pod's z-axis, plus a spine glow strip rod along the top. Then I'm placing sensor details on the pod: lock clamps, a vent cylinder, antenna, and deciding where to mount a rear remote twin gun turret versus keeping the main turret on the cab roof.

I'm defining a reusable turret function that takes a name, base position, scale, and a direction sign so barrels can point forward for the cab or backward for the rear mount. Now I'm planning decal textures—a sealed emblem, unit number, hazard stripes, and a screen—plus writing the paint function that detects panel seams on the hull based on periodic spacing.

Still writing paint logic...

Adding fenders over each wheel, a magenta/cyan roof lightbar, and setting up a turret function with yaw/pitch joints and positioning parameters.
